name: Minicor

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Current applicable tariff unverified
plans.note: Usage-based: pay per successful task (job) execution; development/teaching is included. No public price: no pricing page (minicor.com/pricing 404), sales via 'Book a demo'. Not a per-VM-hour tariff: Minicor-provisioned cloud Windows desktops or customer-owned machines/VPC/on-prem.

caveats: Public enterprise desktop-automation product; YC explicitly says scalable Windows desktop automation/VM. Quote-led offering, no verified Windows CPU/RAM/license-inclusive tariff. Product website sign-in/demo does not prove self-serve availability.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

own_agent_api.quote: `publish_job`, `get_build_status`, `answer_build_question`, `cancel_build`: go live, follow the builder, answer its questions.
own_agent_api.note: Only Minicor's own builder agent (teach_job starts it from a description plus a sample; follow status, answer its questions, cancel) via the Minicor MCP (hosted https://mcp.minicor.com/mcp) and the co-pilot. The builder runs in Minicor's platform and drives the Windows desktop; live jobs are deterministic code triggered by one HTTP call. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosting. The MCP also lets you 'create and manage on-demand, scheduled, or monitoring agents'.

harness_api.quote: `publish_job`, `get_build_status`, `answer_build_question`, `cancel_build`: go live, follow the builder, answer its questions.
harness_api.note: Only Minicor's own builder agent (teach_job starts it from a description plus a sample; follow status, answer its questions, cancel) via the Minicor MCP (hosted https://mcp.minicor.com/mcp) and the co-pilot. The builder runs in Minicor's platform and drives the Windows desktop; live jobs are deterministic code triggered by one HTTP call. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosting. The MCP also lets you 'create and manage on-demand, scheduled, or monitoring agents'.

secret_proxy.quote: Key-value settings resolved into a job at run time. Credentials live here, not in the automation.
secret_proxy.note: Credential vault ('Configurations') plus 2FA/OTP secrets referenced by ID; values are resolved into the run and typed into the target desktop app on the VM, so they do reach the machine. No outbound-request credential-injection proxy.

isolation.quote: Minicor provisions a Windows VM with the Desktop Service installed, the fastest way to start. Or install the Desktop Service on a machine you control: your cloud project, your VPC, or on premises.
isolation.note: Product provisions dedicated Windows VMs (or runs on customer-controlled machines/VPC/on-prem); no specific hypervisor (Hyper-V/KVM/etc.) is named, so exact virtualization layer is unconfirmed.

image_oci.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Machines are Windows desktops/VMs running the Minicor Desktop Service, not container images started from an OCI/Docker image.

anti_bot.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Minicor automates legacy desktop/EHR/ERP software with the account's own login, not evading bot detection on public websites.

captcha_solving.quote: Virtual phones, emails, and authenticator secrets, so a login challenge never needs a person on call.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Minicor solves 2FA/OTP login challenges for the target app, but no CAPTCHA-solving service is documented.

ssh.quote: For extended work on the machine, connect over RDP as usual.
ssh.note: Windows machines are accessed via RDP, not SSH; SSH is not documented anywhere.

snapshot.quote: Minicor provisions a Windows VM with the Desktop Service installed, the fastest way to start.
snapshot.note: No snapshot/checkpoint feature (disk or memory) for desktops is documented anywhere in the docs.

snapshot_auto.quote: Minicor provisions a Windows VM with the Desktop Service installed, the fastest way to start.
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: no automatic state-save/restore documented; product is not modeled around ephemeral suspend/resume machines.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Minicor provisions a Windows VM with the Desktop Service installed, the fastest way to start.

fork.quote: Scaling ... Horizontal Scaling: orchestration across thousands of desktops
fork.note: Scaling is done by provisioning more Windows desktops, not by cloning/forking an existing machine's state; no fork/clone feature documented.

fork_running.quote: Horizontal Scaling: orchestration across thousands of desktops
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no live-clone-a-running-machine feature documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Horizontal Scaling: orchestration across thousands of desktops
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

persistent_disk.quote: Minicor provisions a Windows VM with the Desktop Service installed ... the desktop appears in your workspace with a live preview, ready for jobs.
persistent_disk.note: Cloud desktops are provisioned as persistent VMs the target application is installed on (not ephemeral per-run containers), so files/installed software survive between runs.

volume_shared.quote: A desktop is a Windows machine that runs the application you are automating.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; each desktop is a distinct Windows machine, no shared-volume feature documented.

live_resize.quote: A desktop is a Windows machine that runs the application you are automating.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no CPU/RAM live-resize capability documented for desktops.

agent_harnesses.quote: Minicor exposes a Model Context Protocol server. Point Cursor, Claude Code, or any MCP-capable agent at it and the agent can teach jobs, run samples, inspect failures, drive desktops, and take jobs live.
agent_harnesses.note: Coding agents like Claude Code/Cursor connect TO Minicor's MCP from the user's own machine to control the platform; they are not preinstalled/hosted as templates inside the Windows desktop itself.

lang_python.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
lang_python.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Minicor is a desktop-automation/RPA platform driving GUI apps via clicks/keystrokes/screen reads, not a general Python/Node code-execution runtime.

lang_node.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, same reasoning as lang_python.

inbound_https.quote: One HTTP call to the trigger URL. JSON in, structured JSON out, sync or async.
inbound_https.note: Jobs are triggered via HTTPS trigger URLs served by Minicor's jobs engine (an API endpoint reaching the automation), not a raw exposed desktop port, but it is an inbound HTTPS surface.

ingress_rules.quote: All requests to a trigger URL authenticate with an API key in the `x-api-key` header.
ingress_rules.note: Access to trigger URLs is gated by an API key (an auth-based ingress control), which is provider-side control of who can reach a job endpoint.

egress_allowlist.quote: We provide a complete allowlist of every endpoint the deployment talks to, in both directions, so your network team can pin the boundary down and audit it.
egress_allowlist.note: Documented for the BYOC/on-your-cloud deployment mode.

gpu.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Product is Windows desktop-automation VMs for driving legacy GUI apps; no GPU machine offering is documented.

macos.quote: Windows 10 or later. Open an elevated PowerShell window and paste:
macos.note: The Desktop Service, and thus the whole platform, requires a Windows machine; no macOS support.

arm64.quote: Windows 10 or later. Open an elevated PowerShell window and paste:
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Legacy Windows desktop software targeted (EHR/ERP/DMS/WMS) runs on x86 Windows; no ARM64 offering documented.

open_source.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents
open_source.note: No OSI-licensed core product; Minicor is a closed commercial SaaS/BYOC platform. No public GitHub org with the core engine found.

eu_data_residency.quote: you enter your email, password, and region (US or Canada), and the connection acts as your account
eu_data_residency.note: The only account regions mentioned anywhere are US and Canada; no EU region is documented for the standard hosted platform (BYOC deployments could theoretically be placed in a customer's EU cloud project, but that is not an EU-residency guarantee from Minicor itself).

docker_inside.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Minicor's unit of compute is a Windows desktop VM driven by screen/keyboard automation (docs.minicor.com/running/desktops); no docs mention a container runtime exposed to customers.

nested_virt.quote: A desktop is a Windows machine that runs the application you are automating. Every job executes against a desktop, and everything the automation does happens there.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The Windows machine exists to host the target legacy application for automation, not to run customer-provisioned VMs/emulators inside it; no /dev/kvm or nested hypervisor feature is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Stops are cooperative. There is no pause. Stopping a run lets the current operation finish; plan around that for long automations.
pause_resume.note: Docs explicitly say a run cannot be paused (only stopped). No separate VM-level pause/resume-for-billing feature is documented; billing is per successful job execution, not per VM-hour, and desktops are described as persistently connected machines.

wake_on_request.quote: Once the service is running, the desktop appears in your workspace with a live preview, ready for jobs.
wake_on_request.note: No autoscaling/sleep-and-wake behavior is documented; a desktop must already be connected (its Desktop Service running) to accept a job, with no mention of the platform waking a stopped machine when a trigger call arrives.

volume_attach.quote: A platform for building and running desktop automations at scale with computer use agents.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Minicor exposes jobs (HTTP trigger URLs) and Windows desktops for UI automation, not block-storage/volume management; no attachable-volume feature is documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: One desktop is enough to build and go live. When volume grows, add more desktops and Minicor distributes work across them.
auto_stop_idle.note: Desktops are described as persistently connected machines that queue/serialize jobs; no idle-timeout auto-stop/sleep behavior is documented for either Minicor-provisioned or self-hosted desktops.

egress_http_rules.quote: We provide a complete allowlist of every endpoint the deployment talks to, in both directions, so your network team can pin the boundary down and audit it.
egress_http_rules.note: The documented allowlist covers Minicor's own coordination traffic in a BYOC deployment (network team pins it via their own edge/WAF), not a first-party provider feature letting customers set HTTP method/path-level egress rules on the desktop VM itself.

guest_firewall.quote: Windows 10 or later. Open an elevated PowerShell window and paste: ... irm https://minicor.com/installs/desktop-service/ps1
guest_firewall.note: derived: installing the Desktop Service requires an elevated (administrator) PowerShell session on the Windows machine, implying admin-level control of the guest OS, including its built-in firewall (Windows Defender Firewall). Not documented as a customer-facing feature in its own right.

max_session_h.quote: One desktop is enough to build and go live. When volume grows, add more desktops and Minicor distributes work across them.
max_session_h.note: derived: desktops are persistent Windows VMs that stay connected indefinitely (no auto_stop_idle, no documented idle/session timeout); job runs on them are cooperative-stop only ('Stops are cooperative. There is no pause.', docs.minicor.com/agents/job-build-loop), with no platform-imposed maximum run/session duration documented.
